newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria creates structural reform council.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria creates structural reform council.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim government agreed on Thursday to set up a Structural Reform Council to deal with industrial sector reforms pledged to the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
A statement from the government press centre linked creation of the council to the arrival of a World Bank mission, due in Sofia on Friday to negotiate new loans.

"The priorities of the Council are the estimation of strategic economic objectives, including privatisation, foreign investment, imports and exports, and restructuring on a regional and industrial scale," Industry Minister Alexander Bozhkov, the head of the council, told reporters.

Members of the Stuctural Reform Council are the ministers of finance, transport, trade, agriculture, environment, labour and social care, and the head of the economic department in the interim cabinet, Dimitar Bachvarov.

The Council staff also includes the head of the Securities and Stock Exchange Commission Hristian Tanushev, the managing directors of the Privatisation Agency and the Mass Privatisation Centre Veselin Blagoev and Pirin Atanasov, and the inustrial minister advisor Mladen Georgiev.
The World Bank said on Tuesday its funding was linked to Bulgaria's ability to speed up the reform needed to hasten economic stabilisation.
The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund postponed funding last year after the former Socialist government failed to meet reform targets.
An IMF negotiation mission is also expected to arrive next week.
